So that staff can see who called the most
So rooms are not double-booked or left empty
So that the system needs no password

essays.stem: Describe how to take a telephone reservation, from answering the call to ending it.
essays.modelAnswer: I answer within three rings with a smile in my voice: "Good morning, villa reservations, Kerry-Ann speaking. How may I help you?" I ask for the arrival and departure dates, the number of adults and children, and the type of room or villa wanted, and check availability. I offer suitable choices with the rate, in US$ or J$ as the guest asks, saying whether tax at the current rate and meals are included. When the guest chooses, I take their full name (spelled back), phone number, email, ETA and any special requests. I explain the deposit or guarantee needed and the cancellation terms, and take card details only into the secure system. I read all the details back, give a confirmation number and tell the guest when the written confirmation will arrive. I thank them by name and let them hang up first. Then I check and save the booking.
markingPoints: Answers promptly and politely, naming the property and self
Finds dates, guests and room type and checks availability
Quotes rates clearly with tax, meals and currency
Takes full guest details and requests; explains guarantee and cancellation; card details only into the secure system
Reads back, gives a confirmation number, thanks the caller and saves the booking

essays.stem: Explain what information must be recorded for a reservation, and why each item matters.
essays.modelAnswer: The guest's full name, spelled correctly, is needed to find the booking and greet the guest. The arrival and departure dates, and so the number of nights, decide which room is held and what is charged. The number of adults and children shows the right room and the beds needed. The room or villa type and the rate, with the meal plan and the currency, show what was agreed, so that there is no argument later. The contact details, such as the phone number and email, let the property send a confirmation and contact the guest about changes. The guarantee or deposit and the cancellation terms protect the property against no-shows. The ETA and special requests, such as a cot or an airport transfer, let staff prepare. The source of the booking and the name of the staff member who took it show who to contact and who to ask if there is a problem.
markingPoints: Full name: to find the booking and greet the guest
Dates and nights: decide the room held and the charge
Number of guests, room type, rate, meal plan and currency: what was agreed
Contact details, guarantee or deposit and cancellation terms
ETA, special requests, source and staff name: so that staff can prepare and follow up

essays.stem: Explain the difference between guaranteed and non-guaranteed reservations, and how deposits and release times are used.
essays.modelAnswer: A guaranteed reservation is secured with a card, a deposit or an agreement with a company or travel agent. The property promises to hold the room all night, even if the guest arrives very late. In return, if the guest does not arrive and does not cancel in time, the property may charge a no-show fee, such as one night, as its policy says. A non-guaranteed reservation has no payment behind it. The property holds the room only until a set release time, often 6 p.m. on the day of arrival. If the guest has not arrived or called by then, the room may be released and sold to someone else. A deposit is part of the price paid in advance. It secures the booking and helps cover the loss if the guest cancels late. Guests must be told the guarantee, deposit, release time and cancellation terms clearly when they book.
markingPoints: Guaranteed: secured by card, deposit or agreement; room held all night
No-show fee may be charged under the policy
Non-guaranteed: held only until a release time, such as 6 p.m.
After the release time the room may be sold
Deposit secures the booking and covers late cancellation; terms explained to the guest

essays.stem: Describe how to deal with a guest's request to change (amend) a reservation.
essays.modelAnswer: First, I greet the guest and ask for their name and confirmation number, and I check that I am speaking to the guest or the person who made the booking. I find the booking and ask what they want to change, such as the dates, the number of guests or the room type. I check that the new dates or room are free for every night. I tell the guest if the rate changes, in the right currency, and whether any fee or new deposit applies under the policy. If they agree, I make the change in the system, and I update any special requests, such as a transfer time or a cot, and tell the departments concerned. I read the new details back to the guest, and send a new confirmation that shows the changes. I record the date, the change and my name in the booking notes.
markingPoints: Finds the booking by name and confirmation number; checks it is the guest
Checks availability for the new details
Explains any change in rate, fee or deposit
Updates the booking and requests, and tells the departments concerned
Reads back, sends a new confirmation and records the change

essays.stem: Describe how to deal with a cancellation, including the cancellation policy and the records kept.
essays.modelAnswer: I greet the guest politely and ask for their name, the dates and the confirmation number, and check that I am speaking to the guest or the booker. I find the booking and read back the details so that the right booking is cancelled. I check the cancellation policy and explain it politely: for example, the deposit may be kept if the cancellation is within a set number of days of arrival, or there may be no charge. I do not change the policy myself; if the guest asks for an exception, I refer them to the supervisor. I cancel the booking in the system and give the guest a cancellation number, then send a written cancellation notice. I note the date, time, reason if given, any refund or charge and my name. I make the room available again, and offer it to anyone on the waiting list. I may also invite the guest to book again another time.
markingPoints: Finds and checks the booking with the guest
Explains the cancellation policy politely; refers exceptions to the supervisor
Cancels in the system and gives a cancellation number and written notice
Records date, time, reason, refund or charge and staff name
Releases the room and offers it to the waiting list

essays.topic: Full house, waiting lists and no-shows
essays.stem: Explain how you would deal with a booking request when the property is fully booked for the dates the guest wants.
essays.modelAnswer: I would thank the guest and explain politely that the property is full on those dates, without blaming anyone. I would then try to help. I would check whether other dates close to those asked are free, or whether a different room type is free, and offer these with the rate. If the guest can only come on those dates, I would offer to put them on the waiting list, take their details and tell them how and when I will contact them if a room becomes free, without promising one. If the policy allows, I could suggest a partner villa or property nearby. I would stay calm and friendly even if the guest is upset. I would record the request, because it shows the manager how many guests were turned away. Finally, I would thank the guest for calling and invite them to book again in future.
markingPoints: Explains politely that the property is full
Offers other dates or room types
Offers the waiting list without promising a room
Suggests a partner property if the policy allows; stays calm
Records the request (turn-aways) and thanks the guest

essays.stem: Describe how you would process a group reservation, such as eight rooms for a wedding party.
essays.modelAnswer: I would take the organiser's name and contact details and find out the dates, the number of rooms and room types, the number of guests, and who will pay: one master account, each guest, or a mix. I would check availability for every night and, with the manager, agree the group rate and the terms. I would block the rooms in the system as an allotment, with a cut-off date by which the organiser must give the names, after which unused rooms are released. I would send a written contract or confirmation showing the rooms, rates, deposit, payment plan, cut-off and cancellation terms. Before the cut-off, I would ask for the rooming list with each guest's name and room sharing, and enter the names. I would note special requests, such as late arrivals, a welcome drink or diet needs, and tell the other departments in good time.
markingPoints: Takes the organiser's details, dates, rooms, guests and who pays
Checks availability and agrees the group rate with the manager
Blocks the rooms with a cut-off date for release
Sends a written confirmation or contract with deposit and cancellation terms
Gets the rooming list, enters the names and passes on requests to other departments

essays.stem: Explain how to protect guests' privacy and card details when taking and keeping reservations.
essays.modelAnswer: Guest information belongs to the guest. I would never tell a caller or visitor whether a person has a booking, their dates or their room; I would offer to take a message instead. When taking a booking, I would only ask for the information the property needs. Card details are given only to guarantee or pay for the booking, and I would type them straight into the secure system, never write them on paper, read them aloud where others can hear, or send them by open email. If a guest emails card details, I would follow the property's policy to delete them and ask for a safer way. The reservation system is protected by my own password, which I never share, and I lock the screen when I leave the desk. Printed lists, such as arrivals lists, are kept out of sight and shredded when no longer needed.
markingPoints: Never confirms a guest's booking, dates or room to others; offers to take a message
Asks only for the information needed
Card details only into the secure system; never written, read aloud or emailed openly
Own password, never shared; screen locked
Printed lists kept out of sight and shredded

essays.topic: Quoting prices in J$ and US$
essays.stem: Explain how to quote prices for a reservation correctly, including the currency, tax, deposit and cancellation terms.
essays.modelAnswer: I would use only the property's current rate sheet and quote the right rate for the room type, dates and number of guests, saying whether it is per room or per person, and per night. I would say which meal plan is included, such as EP or all-inclusive. I would quote in the currency the guest asks for. Many villas price in US$; if the guest wants J$, I would use only the rate the property sets for that day and say that the J$ amount may change. I would say clearly whether GCT and any service charge are included or added at the current rate, so that the guest is not surprised. I would explain the deposit, how and when to pay it, and the cancellation terms. Finally, I would put everything in the written confirmation, so that the guest and the property have the same record.
markingPoints: Uses the current rate sheet; per room or person, per night
States the meal plan included
Correct currency; the property's exchange rate only, for that day
States whether GCT and service charge are included, at the current rate
Explains deposit and cancellation terms, and confirms everything in writing

essays.topic: Full house, waiting lists and no-shows
essays.stem: Explain why overbooking and no-shows are problems for a property, and how careful reservations work helps to reduce them.
essays.modelAnswer: A no-show leaves a room empty that could have been sold, so the property loses money. Some properties overbook to cover no-shows, but if every guest arrives, someone has no room. That guest is upset, the property must pay to move them to another property, and its name is harmed. Careful work helps. Staff should ask for a guarantee or deposit and explain the cancellation and no-show terms clearly, so guests are more likely to cancel in time. They should reconfirm bookings a few days before arrival by phone or email. Bookings that are not guaranteed should be released at the release time. Cancellations and changes must be entered at once, so the system is correct and rooms are not double-booked. Keeping a waiting list means a cancelled room can be resold quickly. Managers can use past no-show records to decide how many rooms, if any, to overbook.
markingPoints: No-shows: empty rooms and lost money
Overbooking can leave a guest without a room: cost, upset guest, harm to the property's name
Guarantees or deposits with clear terms; reconfirm before arrival
Release non-guaranteed rooms on time; enter changes and cancellations at once
Use a waiting list and past records

practical1.title: Take and record reservations by phone and email (role play)
practical1.brief: Set up a reservations desk in the Centre's training room with a phone (or a role-play phone card), the Centre's training reservation system or a paper reservation chart for a made-up villa property (for example eight rooms and two villas), a rate sheet in US$, reservation forms and confirmation templates. The assessor gives a made-up exchange rate and a made-up tax rate for the practical, and scenario cards: a couple wanting a double room for 5 nights; a family of 2 adults and 2 children wanting connecting rooms; a returning guest who wants a villa with a cook; a company booking at a corporate rate; and an email request from the USA with the date written 03/04. Each member in turn takes one reservation from a "caller" (another member or the assessor): greets, checks availability, quotes the rate in US$ and J$ with the tax at the given rate, takes and reads back all the details, explains the deposit and cancellation terms, gives a confirmation number, updates the chart or system and writes the confirmation. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, forms, chart and confirmations to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A desk, a phone (or role-play phone card) and a computer with the Centre's training reservation system, or a paper reservation chart
A made-up rate sheet in US$, and a made-up exchange rate and tax rate (from the assessor)
Reservation forms, confirmation templates, a calculator and pens
A phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The reservations desk set up with the chart or system and the rate sheet
Each member taking a reservation call
The rate worked out in US$ and J$ with tax
The chart or system screen updated after each booking
checklist: Answered politely, naming the property and themselves
Found the dates, number of guests and room type, and checked availability
Worked out the number of nights and the cost correctly, in US$ and J$, with the tax at the given rate
Took the full name (spelled back), contact details, ETA and special requests
Explained the deposit or guarantee and the cancellation terms clearly
Read the details back and gave a confirmation number
Updated the chart or system correctly, with no double booking
Kept the card details and guest details private
safety: Use only made-up guest names, card numbers and contact details
Sit correctly at the screen and take short breaks from it
Keep cables and bags clear of walkways
Shred or return all practice papers with guest details at the end

practical2.title: Process changes, cancellations and a group booking, and prepare the arrivals list
practical2.brief: Start from the reservation chart or system the assessor sets up for a made-up villa property, with bookings already made. The assessor gives change cards: a guest who changes their dates; a guest who adds a child and needs a cot; a guest who cancels inside the cancellation period; a guest who cancels in good time; a caller who wants dates that are full (offer other dates or the waiting list); a non-guaranteed booking that has not arrived by the release time; and a wedding group of six rooms with a cut-off date and a rooming list. Each member deals with at least one change card as a role play or by email, follows the policy, updates the chart or system, records the change with a confirmation or cancellation number, and writes the new confirmation or cancellation notice. As a group, block the group rooms and enter the rooming list. Finally, prepare the arrivals list for a date the assessor gives, and work out the occupancy for that night. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and papers to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A reservation chart or the Centre's training system with made-up bookings (from the assessor)
Change cards, the cancellation policy and a made-up rooming list (from the assessor)
Confirmation and cancellation templates, a waiting list form and an arrivals list form
A calculator, pens and a phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The chart or system before any changes
Each change being handled, with the record or note
Each new confirmation or cancellation notice
The waiting list with the caller's details
The group rooms blocked and the rooming list entered
The finished arrivals list and the occupancy sum
The chart or system after all the changes
checklist: Found the right booking using the name and confirmation number
Checked availability before agreeing any change
Applied the cancellation policy correctly and politely
Gave and recorded a confirmation or cancellation number
Offered other dates or the waiting list without promising a room
Released the non-guaranteed room correctly at the release time
Entered the group block and rooming list correctly
Prepared a correct arrivals list and worked out the occupancy correctly
safety: Use only made-up guest names and details
Sit correctly at the screen and take short breaks from it
Keep the work area tidy and cables clear
Shred or return all practice papers with guest details at the end
